plan.title: Round Solid-Pine Side Table
plan.summary: A 600 mm diameter pine side table with a solid round top, four outward-splayed tapered legs, and four underside mounting cleats. The reference drawing shows a shorter overall height; the legs are lengthened to meet your 600 mm target.
assumptions: The target dimensions take priority over the drawing: the tabletop is 25 mm thick, so its underside is 575 mm above the floor.
The reference drawing's 7° leg splay is interpreted as each leg leaning outward radially. Cleat centers are 112 mm from the table center; the leg centerlines spread another 68 mm toward the floor.
The top is cut from a 25 mm solid, edge-glued pine panel. A single 600 mm-wide solid pine board is not assumed.
The four legs are solid-pine turned tapers, 40 mm diameter at the top and 28 mm at the foot. Buy turned legs to these dimensions, or have them turned; custom legs may not be available off the shelf.
Leg centerline endpoints and lengths define the layout. The level-cut feet sit on the floor; the upper ends meet the underside cleats. Leg-to-cleat contact and fasteners are intentional joinery.

parts.name: Round tabletop
parts.notes: Cut a 600 mm diameter circle. The placement box is its circular bounding square.

parts.name: Tapered splayed leg
parts.notes: 557.2 mm is the centerline length: √(553² + 68²). Taper from 40 mm at the upper end to 28 mm at the foot. Ends are cut level so they meet the horizontal cleat and floor.

parts.name: Leg mounting cleat
parts.notes: One cleat beneath each leg, centered on its upper centerline. Round the corners to reduce sharp edges.

hardware.name: Wood screws for cleats to tabletop
hardware.notes: Two per cleat, driven upward through the cleat. Confirm screw tips will not break through the 25 mm tabletop.

hardware.name: Structural wood screws for legs to cleats
hardware.notes: Two per leg, driven through the cleat into the leg with angled pilot holes. Use screws rated for structural wood connections.

hardware.name: Wood glue
hardware.notes: One small bottle; use a thin layer at leg-to-cleat contact. Do not rely on glue alone.

finishes.name: Clear water-based polyurethane
finishes.notes: Apply 2–3 thin coats to the top and legs, including the underside and feet. Follow the product label for sanding and recoat times.

tools.name: Compass or trammel for marking a 600 mm circle
tools.alternative: A string-and-pencil compass with a securely fixed center point.

tools.name: Jigsaw with a fine wood blade
tools.alternative: Ask a cabinet shop to cut the circle, or use a router with a circle-cutting jig.

tools.name: Drill/driver and countersink bit
tools.alternative: A hand drill and manual countersink can be used more slowly.

tools.name: Clamps
tools.alternative: Use a helper to hold parts securely while drilling; do not hold small pieces by hand near a bit.

tools.name: Miter saw or handsaw with a square cutting guide
tools.alternative: Have the leg supplier cut the feet level to the specified splay.

tools.name: PPE: safety glasses, hearing protection, and dust mask

steps.title: Check the leg stock and layout
steps.text: Confirm P2 (tapered splayed legs) are 557.2 mm along their centerlines, taper from 40 mm to 28 mm, and can be cut with level ends. Mark the tabletop center and the four leg/cleat centerlines 112 mm out from the center in the left, right, front, and back directions. If buying legs, have the supplier confirm the level cuts suit the 68 mm outward splay over a 553 mm drop.
steps.tip: The cleat centers are not at the tabletop edge; keeping them at the specified radius leaves ample room inside the top.

steps.title: Cut the round tabletop
steps.text: Mark a 600 mm diameter circle on P1 (round tabletop), then cut just outside the line with a jigsaw. Sand back to the line until the edge is smooth and round. If you are not comfortable cutting a large circle, have a cabinet shop cut it.
tools_used: Compass or trammel for marking a 600 mm circle
Jigsaw with a fine wood blade
steps.safety: Wear eye, hearing, and dust protection. Clamp the panel securely, keep hands clear of the blade, and support the offcut so it cannot pinch the blade.
steps.tip: Make the cut in a stable, supported panel and avoid forcing the jigsaw around the curve.

steps.title: Prepare the cleats
steps.text: Cut four P3 (leg mounting cleats) to size and round their corners. Mark each cleat's center and drill two 4 mm clearance holes for its tabletop screws. Keep the holes far enough from the edges to avoid splitting.
tools_used: Miter saw or handsaw with a square cutting guide
steps.safety: Wear eye protection when cutting or drilling; clamp each cleat before working on it.
steps.tip: Keep the screw holes clear of the area where the leg will meet the cleat.

steps.title: Mark the underside
steps.text: Place P1 (round tabletop) upside down on a padded, flat surface. Transfer the four radial centerlines from step 1 and position one P3 (leg mounting cleat) at each center, with its long direction radial to the table center. Check that each leg centerline will land at the cleat center and that all four positions are symmetric.
steps.tip: Measure from the table center rather than from the circular edge, which is easy to misjudge.

steps.title: Attach the cleats
steps.text: Apply a thin layer of glue to each P3 (leg mounting cleat), then fasten it to the underside of P1 (round tabletop) with two 4 × 35 mm screws. Keep each cleat aligned with its radial mark and pre-drill if the pine is prone to splitting. Wipe away squeezed-out glue and let it set according to the glue label.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and keep the driver bit straight to avoid slipping. Do not overtighten screws into pine.
steps.tip: Check screw length on a scrap stack of 22 mm cleat plus 25 mm top before assembly; the screw must not emerge through the tabletop.

steps.title: Dry-fit and orient the legs
steps.text: Fit each P2 (tapered splayed leg) against the underside of its P3 (leg mounting cleat). Orient them so their upper centerlines sit 112 mm from the table center and their feet lean outward, ending 180 mm from the center. Check that the four feet sit level and the top stands at 600 mm before fastening.
steps.tip: Do not trim legs until you have checked all four positions; small differences are noticeable on a round table.

steps.title: Pilot-drill the leg connections
steps.text: With the tabletop still upside down, clamp each P2 (tapered splayed leg) to its P3 (leg mounting cleat). Drill two angled pilot holes through each cleat into the leg, keeping the holes spaced apart and centered on solid wood. Use a bit sized for the screw's core, and avoid drilling through the top.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection, clamp the work, and keep both hands clear of the drill path. Stop if a pilot hole approaches an edge or risks breaking through the tabletop.
steps.tip: Test the angle and pilot-hole size on a scrap block before drilling the finished legs.

steps.title: Fasten the legs
steps.text: Apply a thin layer of glue where each P2 (tapered splayed leg) meets its P3 (leg mounting cleat). Drive two 6 × 70 mm structural screws through each cleat into its leg, tightening until snug without crushing the pine. Keep the legs clamped while the glue cures; follow the glue label for clamp time.
steps.safety: Wear eye protection and use a driver setting that prevents the screw from snapping or stripping. The upside-down assembly is awkward; get help to turn it after the glue cures.
steps.tip: If a leg shifts as the first screw tightens, back it off, realign it, and retighten before adding the second screw.

steps.title: Level and sand the table
steps.text: Turn the table upright with a helper and check that all four feet contact the floor. If needed, have a careful, small correction made to the foot cuts while keeping them level. Sand P1 (round tabletop), P2 (tapered splayed legs), and exposed P3 (leg mounting cleats) through 120, 180, then 220 grit; ease sharp tabletop edges slightly.
tools_used: Miter saw or handsaw with a square cutting guide
steps.safety: Get help lifting and turning the assembly. Wear eye and dust protection when sanding; keep loose clothing and fingers away from moving tools.
steps.tip: Check for rocking on a flat floor before applying finish; finish will not correct uneven feet.

steps.title: Apply the finish
steps.text: Remove all sanding dust and apply a thin coat of clear water-based polyurethane to P1 (round tabletop), P2 (tapered splayed legs), and exposed P3 (leg mounting cleats). Let it dry for the label's stated time, lightly sand between coats as directed, and apply 2–3 coats. Coat the underside and feet as well as visible surfaces.
steps.safety: Work with good ventilation, wear gloves and any PPE required by the finish label, and keep finishes away from flames. Dispose of finish-soaked rags according to the product instructions.
steps.tip: Test the finish on a pine offcut first; pine can absorb finish unevenly.

safety_overview: Wear safety glasses and hearing protection for cutting and drilling; wear a dust mask when sanding.
Clamp panels and small cleats securely. Keep hands clear of saw blades and drill bits, and never force a cut.
Use a helper to turn or carry the assembled table; it is awkward to handle upside down.
Use finish only with good ventilation and follow its label for PPE, drying, and rag disposal.
Check the table for rocking and secure leg connections before putting weight on it.
